The only change to .github/workflows/ci.yml is a new step in the release-integrity job. The step at head lines 62-63 runs `python3 scripts/test_model_registry_workflow.py`, a loopback-HTTP test.

The job keeps its existing settings:
- workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` (head line 8–9)
- no secrets
- the same runner
- triggers of push and pull_request, with no pull_request_target

Within this job, the new step adds no privilege or secret exposure. The test script itself was not supplied, so its contents and any network use beyond loopback were not reviewed.

For .github/workflows/register-model.yml (unit ed2ebf29ce779637:0), only metadata was supplied: modified, mode 100644 unchanged. No patch or source text was supplied, which is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. The next pass must examine:
- register-model.yml triggers (workflow_dispatch vs pull_request_target)
- permissions
- use of secrets
- untrusted input interpolated into `run:` steps

These matter because model registration may affect the coordinator model catalog and weight-hash expectations (T-012, T-027, A-004), and possibly the release key (A-005) and hash registry (A-011) if the workflow uses coordinator API keys.

No provider runtime, attestation, encryption or cache code changed in the supplied units. T-041 is not affected.
